name: Climate Change
miniText: The scientific question is whether radiative absorption, reflection and escape change the Earths modeled energy balance. In NetLogo's Climate Change model, sunlight becomes stored heat or reflected energy, and emitted infrared packets interact with greenhouse-gas and cloud representations. The selected literature connects this mechanism to greenhouse forcing and energy balance: the original carbon-dioxide calculation connects atmospheric composition to temperature [1]; radiative-convective equilibrium provides a physically richer atmospheric comparison [2]; forcing efficacy qualifies simple equivalence between different climate perturbations [3]. Packet collisions and one surface temperature are teaching abstractions; the display does not resolve molecular spectroscopy, ocean circulation or regional climate change. The original NetLogo behavior is the baseline for reimplementation. This simulation offers a controlled thought experiment, and agreement with its output does not establish empirical validation.

verification.evidenceSummary: We use a global climate model to compare the effectiveness of many climate forcing agents for producing climate change. We find a substantial range in the “efficacy” of different forcings, where the efficacy is the global temperature response per unit forcing relative to the response to CO 2 forcing. Anthropogenic CH 4 has efficacy ∼110%, which increases to ∼145% when its indirect effects on stratospheric H 2 O and tropospheric O 3 are included, yielding an effective climate forcing of ∼0.8 W/m 2 for the period 1750–2000 and making CH 4 the largest anthropogenic climate forcing other than CO 2 . Black carbon (BC) aerosols from biomass burning have a calculated efficacy ∼58%, while fossil fuel BC has an efficacy ∼78%.
